extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, trademark/geographical indication applicants, IP practitioners and businesses seeking industrial property protection in Vietnam
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory criteria and procedural requirements under Vietnamese industrial property law for registrability, validity, maintenance, amendment, invalidation and application content for inventions, designs, marks, geographical indications, layout-designs and business secrets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs not protected as marks (enumerated exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of signs which shall not be protected as marks, including: signs lacking distinctiveness acquired through use before filing; signs describing legal status and business field of entities; signs indicating geographical origin except widely used/recognized marks or registered collective/certification marks; signs identical or confusingly similar to earlier-filed marks; signs identical/confusingly similar to widely used/recognized marks; signs identical/similar to marks whose registration was invalidated within 5 years (with exceptions); signs identical/similar to well-known marks that affect distinctiveness or take advantage of reputation; signs identical/similar to another’s trade name causing origin confusion; signs identical/similar to protected geographical indications if misleading; signs identical/containing/transcribed from geographical indications for wines/spirits registered for non-originating wines/spirits; signs identical/insignificantly different from another’s industrial design protected by earlier filing/priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerated list (points d through m in the Law) identifies concrete categories of signs that are ineligible for mark protection due to lack of distinctiveness, conflict with prior rights, well-known status, geographic-indication conflicts, or identity/similarity to protected industrial designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluation of well-known marks — consumer awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of involved consumers who have been aware of the mark through purchase or use of goods or services bearing the mark or through advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of eight factors to consider when determining well-known status (Article 75.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluation of well-known marks — territorial area
rubrics_metrics.description: Territorial area in which goods or services bearing the mark are circulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider geographic spread of circulation when assessing well-known status (Article 75.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluation of well-known marks — turnover/quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Turnover of the sale of goods or provision of services bearing the mark or the quantity of goods sold or services provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial scale/sales volume contribute to well-known mark determination (Article 75.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluation of well-known marks — duration of use
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of continuous use of the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length of continuous use is a relevant factor for well-known status (Article 75.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluation of well-known marks — wide reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Wide reputation of goods or services bearing the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market reputation and recognition are considered in well-known mark evaluation (Article 75.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluation of well-known marks — number of countries protecting the mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of countries protecting the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International protection footprint informs well-known status (Article 75.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluation of well-known marks — number of countries recognizing as well-known
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of countries recognizing the mark as a well-known mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition by foreign jurisdictions is relevant to well-known determination (Article 75.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluation of well-known marks — assignment/licensing/investment value
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment price, licensing price, or investment capital contribution value of the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic valuation and transactional evidence of the mark factor into well-known assessment (Article 75.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: General conditions for trade names eligible for protection
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade name shall be protected when it is capable of distinguishing the business entity bearing it from other business entities operating in the same business field and locality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinctiveness in the relevant field and locality is required for trade name protection (Article 76).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters not protected as trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of state agencies, political organizations, socio-political organizations, socio-political-professional organizations, social organizations, socio-professional organizations or other entities that are not involved in business activities shall not be protected as trade names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade name protection excludes non-commercial/public or non-business entities (Article 77).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness of trade names — proper name rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade name shall be considered distinctive when consisting of a proper name, except where it has been widely known through use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper names are distinctive only if widely known by use; otherwise additional distinctiveness required (Article 78.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness of trade names — non-confusion with earlier trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: Not being identical with or confusingly similar to a trade name having been used earlier by another person in the same business field and locality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior use by others in same field/locality bars protection where confusion would result (Article 78.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness of trade names — non-conflict with prior marks/GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Being not identical with or confusingly similar to another person’s mark or a geographical indication having been protected before the date it is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade names must avoid conflict with prior marks or protected geographical indications (Article 78.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: General conditions for geographical indications eligible for protection
rubrics_metrics.description: A geographical indication shall be protected when: (1) the product originates from the area corresponding to the geographical indication; and (2) the product has a reputation, quality or characteristics mainly attributable to geographical conditions of that area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both origin linkage and reputation/quality/characteristics tied to geography are required (Article 79.1-2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters not protected as geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographical indications shall not be protected when: they have become generic names in Vietnam; they are from foreign countries where they are not protected or no longer used; they are identical or similar to a protected mark where use would likely cause confusion as to origin; or they would mislead consumers as to true geographical origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated exclusion grounds (Article 80.1–4) bar GI protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation determination for products bearing geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation shall be determined on the basis of consumers’ trust in such products through the extent of their being widely known to and selected by consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer awareness and selection underpin reputation analysis for GIs (Article 81.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and characteristics criteria for geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and characteristics shall be defined by one or several qualitative, quantitative or physically, chemically, microbiologically perceptible criteria which can be tested by technical means or experts with appropriate testing methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GI descriptions must include testable, expert-evaluable criteria linking product traits to the GI (Article 81.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical conditions relevant to GIs — natural factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural factors include climatic, hydrological, geological, topographical and ecological factors and other natural conditions decisive to reputation, quality and characteristics of products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural environmental elements must be identified where they affect product qualities (Article 82.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical conditions relevant to GIs — human factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Human factors include skills and expertise of producers, and traditional production processes of localities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human-related production methods and skills that shape product characteristics are relevant to GI protection (Article 82.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical areas bearing GIs must be accurately determined
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographical areas bearing geographical indications shall have their boundaries accurately determined in words and maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GI applications must specify precise geographic boundaries both descriptively and cartographically (Article 83).

rubrics_metrics.name: General conditions for business secrets eligible for protection
rubrics_metrics.description: A business secret shall be protected when it: (1) is neither common knowledge nor easily obtained; (2) is capable, when used in business activities, of rendering advantages to its holder; (3) is kept secret by its owner with necessary measures so it is neither disclosed nor easily accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three conditions (novelty/confidentiality, economic advantage, and reasonable secrecy measures) are required for business secret protection (Article 84.1–3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters not protected as business secrets
rubrics_metrics.description: The following confidential information shall not be protected as business secrets: personal identification secrets; state management secrets; national defense and security secrets; other confidential information irrelevant to business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-business or state/national-security categories are excluded from business-secret protection (Article 85).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to register inventions, industrial designs and layout-designs — eligible applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who created inventions/designs with their own efforts and expenses; organizations/individuals who supplied funds and material facilities under job assignment or hiring (unless otherwise agreed); the Government provides for registration rights where created using state budget facilities/funds; jointly-created/invested parties all have registration rights exercised by consensus; registration right may be assigned, bequeathed or inherited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies who has standing to file registration for inventions/designs and rules on assignment and joint creation (Article 86 clauses 1–4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to register marks — eligible applicants and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations or individuals have the right to register marks to be used for goods they produce or services they provide; lawful traders of others’ products can register marks provided producers do not use or object; collective organizations can register collective marks; quality-control organizations can register certification marks if not engaged in production/trading; co-owners may jointly register under conditions (used in names of all co-owners or used for goods/services with co-owners' participation and causing no consumer confusion); registration rights may be assigned with conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed eligibility and constraints for mark registration, including special rules for collective and certification marks and co-ownership (Article 87 clauses 1–7 and subclauses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to register geographical indications — Vietnamese GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to register Vietnamese geographical indications belongs to the State; the State allows organizations/individuals producing products bearing GIs, collective organizations representing them, or administrative management agencies of localities to exercise the right to register; registrants do not become owners of the GI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GIs are state-owned rights with registration exercisable by producers/collectives/admin agencies but without transfer of ownership (Article 88).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of filing registration applications — who must file and representation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Vietnamese orgs/individuals, foreign individuals permanently residing in Vietnam, and foreign orgs/individuals with establishments in Vietnam may file directly or through representatives; foreign individuals not permanently residing and foreign orgs/entities without establishments must file through lawful representatives in Vietnam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines filing modalities depending on applicant residence/establishment status (Article 89 clauses 1–2).

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple applications by different parties are filed for the same invention/design/mark for identical or similar goods/services, protection may only be granted to the valid application with the earliest priority or filing date among those satisfying all grant conditions. If multiple applications have the same earliest priority/filing date and satisfy conditions, a single application may be granted only by agreement of all applicants; without agreement, all are refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes priority by filing/priority date and resolves competing simultaneous filings (Article 90 clauses 1–2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of priority — conditions to claim priority
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may claim priority from a first application if: (a) the first application was filed in Vietnam or a contracting party country; (b) the applicant is a citizen or resident/has establishment in Vietnam or the country of first filing; (c) the claim is clearly stated and a certified copy of the first application is enclosed; (d) the application is filed within the time limit provided in the relevant treaty. Applicants may claim priority from different earlier applications for corresponding contents; the priority date is the filing date of the first application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies documentary and substantive conditions for claiming priority under treaties and bilateral agreements (Article 91 clauses 1–3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection titles — what they recognize and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection titles shall recognize owners of inventions, industrial designs, layout-designs or marks, authors of inventions/designs/layout-designs; they record subject matters, scope and term of protection. For geographical indications, titles record managing organizations, right-to-use entities, protected GI, product characteristics, geographical characteristics and areas. Protection title types include invention patent, utility solution patent, industrial design patent, certificate of registered semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design, certificate of registered mark and certificate of registered geographical indication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines content and categories of protection titles (Article 92 clauses 1–3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity terms for different protection titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection titles valid throughout Vietnam. Invention patents: start at grant, expire at end of 20 years after filing date. Utility solution patents: start at grant, expire at end of 10 years after filing. Industrial design patents: start at grant, expire 5 years after filing and may be renewed for two consecutive 5-year terms. Certificates of registered layout-designs: validity starts at grant and expires at the earliest of: end of 10 years after filing; end of 10 years after first commercial exploitation by right-holder/licensee; end of 15 years after creation. Certificates of registered marks: start at grant, expire 10 years after filing and may be renewed for many consecutive 10-year terms. Certificates of registered geographical indications: indefinite validity starting from grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise statutory terms for each type of protection title and renewal/expiry rules (Article 93 clauses 1–7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and prolongation of validity — fees
rubrics_metrics.description: To maintain validity of invention or utility solution patents, the owner must pay validity maintenance fees. To prolong validity of industrial design patents or certificates of registered marks, the owner must pay validity prolongation fees. Fee rates and procedures are provided by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee payment is mandatory to keep or extend protection; rates/procedures are gov't-prescribed (Article 94 clauses 1–3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of validity — statutory grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A protection title's validity terminates if: (a) owner fails to pay maintenance/prolongation fee as prescribed; (b) owner declares relinquishment; (c) owner no longer exists or owner of a registered mark is no longer engaged in business with no lawful heir; (d) mark not used by owner or licensee without justifiable reasons for 5 consecutive years prior to a request for termination, except where use commenced/resumed at least 3 months before request; (e) owner of a collective mark fails to supervise implementation of usage regulation; (f) owner of a certification mark violates or fails to supervise its use regulation; (g) geographical conditions decisive to reputation/quality/characteristics of products bearing a GI have changed resulting in loss of those attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated specific statutory events that trigger termination of validity; procedures and recording/publishing follow (Article 95 clause 1 and following clauses explaining consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of protection titles — grounds for entire or partial invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: A protection title shall be entirely invalidated if: (a) the registration applicant had neither had nor been assigned the right to register; (b) the subject matter failed to satisfy protection conditions at the time the title was granted. A protection title shall be partly invalidated when that part fails to satisfy protection conditions. Requests may be made to the state agency with fees; statute of limitations for invalidation requests is the whole term of protection (for marks it is 5 years from grant date except where title was granted due to applicant dishonesty). The agency issues decisions on invalidation or refusal after examination and parties' opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies grounds, partial/entire invalidation, time limits and procedural aspects (Article 96 and following paragraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to protection titles — permitted changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners may request amendments to: modifications/error corrections in name and address of author or owner; amendments to description of characteristics/quality/geographical area of GIs; amendments to regulations on use of collective marks or certification marks. The agency must correct its own errors without fee. Owners may request narrowing the scope of rights (requires substantive re-examination and payment of substantive examination fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists amendable information, error-correction rules, and process/costs for scope-narrowing (Article 97 clauses 1–3).

rubrics_metrics.name: National register of industrial property — contents and custody
rubrics_metrics.description: The national register records establishment, change and transfer of industrial property rights to inventions, industrial designs, layout-designs, marks and GIs; decisions on grant, principal contents and decisions on amendment, termination, invalidation, and registration of transfer contracts are recorded. The register is compiled and kept by the state management agency in charge of industrial property rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines official recording obligations and repository for IP title lifecycle events (Article 98 clauses 1–3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of decisions relating to protection titles — timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions on grant, termination of validity, invalidation or amendment of protection titles shall be published in the Official Gazette of Industrial Property within 60 days from date of issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must publish key decisions within statutory 60-day timeframe (Article 99).

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirements on industrial property registration applications — constituent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: An application comprises: (a) a declaration for registration, made according to a set form; (b) documents, samples and information identifying the subject matter as specified in Articles 102–106; (c) power of attorney if filed through a representative; (d) documents evidencing the registration right if acquired from another; (e) documents evidencing the priority right if claimed; (f) vouchers of payment of fees and charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum filing content required for receipt of an application (Article 100 clause 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language rules for applications and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and papers shall be made in Vietnamese, except that certain documents (power of attorney; documents evidencing registration right; documents evidencing priority right; other supporting documents) can be in another language but must be translated into Vietnamese at the request of the state agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary language is Vietnamese; selected supporting docs may be filed in other languages subject to translation on request (Article 100 clause 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents evidencing priority right
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents evidencing priority right include a copy of first application(s) certified by the receiving office and deed of assignment of priority right if acquired from another person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify acceptable documentary proof to support priority claims (Article 100 clause 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement on the uniformity of industrial property registration applications — single subject rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application shall request the grant of only one protection title for a single industrial property subject matter, except where statutory exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General one-subject-per-application rule with enumerated statutory exceptions (Article 101 clause 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — group of technically linked inventions in one application
rubrics_metrics.description: Each registration application may request one invention patent or one utility solution patent for a group of inventions that are technically linked to form a single common inventive idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits filing a linked-group of inventions under one application when they express a single inventive concept (Article 101 clause 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — industrial design multiple-items/variants in one application
rubrics_metrics.description: One industrial design patent may cover several industrial designs where: (a) designs of a set of products express a single common inventive idea and are used together or for a common purpose; (b) an industrial design accompanied by variants that express a single common inventive idea and are not significantly different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows multiple related designs/variants in one application under defined conditions (Article 101 clause 3 a–b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — one mark for multiple goods/services in one application
rubrics_metrics.description: Each registration application may request one certificate of registered mark for one mark to be used for one or more different goods or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks may be registered in one application across multiple classes/goods/services (Article 101 clause 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements on invention registration applications — contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents identifying an invention must include a description and an abstract; the description consists of a description section and the scope of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must include descriptive and scope elements to identify the invention (Article 102.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention description — sufficiency of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of invention must: (a) fully and clearly disclose the nature of the invention to the extent it may be realized by a person with average knowledge in the art; (b) briefly explain accompanied drawings if required; (c) clarify the novelty, inventive step and susceptibility of industrial application of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets written-description/enabling requirement, need to relate to drawings, and requirement to address novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability (Article 102.2 a–c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of protection of inventions — expression and compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of protection shall be expressed in the form of a combination of technical specifications which are necessary and sufficient to identify the scope of the rights, and compatible with the description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims/scope must be technically precise, necessary & sufficient, and consistent with the disclosure (Article 102.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts of inventions — required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts must disclose principal features of the nature of such inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should summarize main technical features (Article 102.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements on industrial design registration applications — documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must include a description and a set of photos or drawings; the description consists of a description section and a scope of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both textual description and visual depiction are required for design filings (Article 103.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design description — completeness and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must: (a) fully disclose all features expressing the nature of the design and clearly identify features which are new and different from the least different known design and be consistent with photos/drawings; (b) when variants exist, fully show variants and distinctions; (c) when design is of a set, fully show features of each product of the set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires comprehensive disclosure of novel/different features, variant distinctions, and set-item features (Article 103.2 a–c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design scope of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope must clearly define features which need to be protected, including features new and different from similar known industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims for design protection must identify protectable novel features (Article 103.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design photos/drawings requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of photos and drawings must fully define features of the industrial design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visuals must completely represent the design for examination (Article 103.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements on layout-design registration applications — required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents identifying a layout-design include: (1) drawings and photos of the layout-design; (2) information on functions and structure of semiconductor integrated circuits produced under the layout-design; (3) samples of semiconductor integrated circuits produced under the layout-design if commercially exploited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies technical drawings/photos, functional/structural information and samples for layout-design filings (Article 104).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements on mark registration applications — identifying documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents include: (a) a sample of the mark and a list of goods or services bearing the mark; (b) regulation on use of collective marks or certification marks (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base documentation for mark filings must include mark sample and goods/services list; collective/certification marks require formal regulations (Article 105.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark sample description, transcription and translation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The sample of the mark must be described to clarify its elements and comprehensive meaning; hieroglyphic words/phrases must be transcribed; foreign language words/phrases must be translated into Vietnamese.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark depiction must include descriptive/transliteration/translation details to ensure clarity in Vietnamese proceedings (Article 105.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of goods/services for mark applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Goods or services listed must be classified into appropriate groups in accordance with the Classification List under the Nice Agreement as published by the state agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use the Nice classification as adopted by the agency for proper classification (Article 105.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation on use of collective marks — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Must include: name/address/grounds of establishment of collective organization; criteria for becoming a member; list of organizations/individuals permitted to use the mark; conditions for use; measures for handling violating acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective mark filings require a governance/regulation document covering membership, permitted users, use conditions and enforcement (Article 105.4 a–e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation on use of certification marks — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Must include: the organization/individual being the mark owner; conditions for using the mark; characteristics of goods/services certified; methods of evaluating characteristics and controlling use; expenses to be paid by mark user for certification/protection, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification mark filings must detail owner, certification criteria, testing/monitoring methods and user costs (Article 105.5 a–e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements on geographical indication registration applications — identifying documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents include: (a) the name or sign being the GI; (b) the product bearing the GI; (c) description of peculiar characteristics/quality/reputation and particular elements of natural conditions decisive to them; (d) map of the geographical area; (e) documents evidencing GI protection in country of origin for foreign GIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GI applications must present name/sign, product, descriptive evidence of characteristics and mapped area; foreign GIs need protection evidence from origin country (Article 106.1 a–e).

rubrics_metrics.name: GI description of peculiar characteristics — principal contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Must contain: (a) description of microbiological and perceptible properties of the product including raw materials and physical/chemical characteristics; (b) method of identification of the geographical area; (c) evidence proving product originates from such area per Article 79; (d) description of local and stable production/processing methods; (e) information on relationship between peculiar characteristics/quality/reputation and geographical conditions; (f) information on mechanism of self-control of the peculiar characteristics or quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GI descriptions must be scientifically and procedurally detailed, linking product traits to area and describing quality control mechanisms (Article 106.2 a–f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized representation — power of attorney formal contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization for procedures must be in writing as a power of attorney and include: full name and address of principal and attorney; scope of authorization; valid term of authorization; date of making the power of attorney; signature and seal (if any) of the principal. A power without a valid term is considered indefinitely valid until principal declares termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies mandatory elements of POAs used in IP procedures and rules on validity term (Article 107 clauses 1–3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt of applications and filing date — minimum contents for receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall only be received if it consists of at least: (a) a declaration for registration including sufficient info to identify applicant and for mark applications a sample of the mark and list of goods/services; (b) a description including scope (for inventions), photos/drawings and description (for designs), description of peculiar characteristics (for GIs); (c) voucher of payment of filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the minimal package required for the agency to accept an application and allocate a filing date (Article 108.1 a–c).
